title: Vertex Form
short: In y = a(x − h)² + k the vertex is (h, k).
trouble: Students read the vertex of y = (x − 2)² + 3 as (−2, 3).

blocks.html: Writing a quadratic as $y = a(x - h)^2 + k$ shows its vertex at a glance. This is the transformation idea applied to $y = x^2$: shift it right $h$, stretch by $a$, shift it up $k$. It makes the features of a parabola easy to read.

A square is never negative, so $(x - h)^2 \ge 0$, and it equals $0$ only when $x = h$. If $a > 0$, then $a(x - h)^2 \ge 0$ too, so $y \ge k$, with $y = k$ exactly at $x = h$: the lowest point is $(h, k)$. If $a < 0$ the inequality flips and $(h, k)$ is the highest point. Either way the vertex is $(h, k)$ and the axis of symmetry is $x = h$.

blocks.name: parabola

opts.task: Move the vertex to $(-1, 4)$ and make the parabola open down.

blocks.cap: Move $h$ and $k$ to slide the vertex; $a$ controls width and direction. Notice that a positive $h$ moves the vertex to the right.

blocks.html: In $y = a(x - h)^2 + k$ the vertex is $(h, k)$: watch the sign, since $x + 3 = x - (-3)$ gives $h = -3$. The axis is $x = h$, and $k$ is the minimum ($a > 0$) or maximum ($a < 0$) value.

blocks.title: Read the vertex
blocks.q: Find the vertex and the maximum or minimum of $y = -2(x + 3)^2 + 5$.
steps: $a = -2 < 0$: opens down, so $5$ is the maximum value.

blocks.title: Write from a vertex and a point
blocks.q: A parabola has vertex $(1, -4)$ and passes through $(3, 4)$. Write its equation.
steps: Use the point: $4 = a(3 - 1)^2 - 4 = 4a - 4$, so $4a = 8$ and $a = 2$.

blocks.html: Reading the vertex of $y = (x - 2)^2 + 3$ as $(-2, 3)$. The form subtracts $h$, so $x - 2$ means $h = +2$. Check: at $x = 2$ the square is $0$ and $y = 3$, the smallest possible value, so $(2, 3)$ is the vertex.
